# SOP-P3-L4-05 Planned shutdown - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03
Related documents: MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2, SOP-P3-L4-01

1. Purpose and scope
   1.1. This procedure defines the planned shutdown sequence for the Heat Treat line (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) and associated roller return (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) and shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). It covers isolation, lubrication, dust control checks and safe restart preparations for scheduled maintenance aligned to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
   1.2. Background and rationale: Planned shutdowns prevent unplanned downtime and reduce risk to personnel and equipment. Coordinated isolation and verification steps reduce the chance of trapped energy, contamination of heat treat atmospheres, and damage to conveyor and blast subsystems. Follow-up records enable trend analysis and support MM-P3-L4-HT02 preventative tasks.

2. Preconditions (must be verified before step 3)
   2.1. Production schedule has authorized line outage per SOP-P3-L4-01.
   2.2. Maintenance work order created and attached to the shutdown record.
   2.3. Notify operations, quality, and safety departments per site notification procedures in SOP-P3-L4-01.
   2.4. Ensure spares and consumables listed in MM-P3-L4-HT02 are on site.
   2.5. Confirm the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. Record this value on the shutdown checklist before isolation.

3. Required PPE
   3.1. Mandatory: flame-resistant coveralls, safety glasses with side shields, heat-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection.
   3.2. For work inside ovens or cabinets: supplied-air respirator if atmosphere monitoring indicates contaminants above action levels per MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2.
   3.3. Lockout/tagout (LOTO) kits and arc flash PPE as required by site LOTO policy referenced in SOP-P3-L4-01.

4. Shutdown sequence (stepwise actions and rationale)
   4.1. Coordinate and confirm line hold. Rationale: prevents inadvertent loading of parts during isolation.
   4.2. Stop material feed and clear workstations. Rationale: ensures no parts are in the heat treat envelope or on conveyors.
   4.3. Isolate power to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-RR01 using approved LOTO procedure. Verify zero energy at specified disconnect points. Rationale: eliminates electrical energy and motion hazard for maintenance crews.
   4.4. Isolate compressed air and any process gas feeds to EQ-P3-L4-HT02. Rationale: prevents unintended flow into the oven atmosphere and hazards to technicians.
   4.5. De-energize and lock out the dust collector serving EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Verify the dust collector pressure drop alarm reading and record; if the recorded alarm differs from the precondition value, flag in the maintenance record and notify the maintenance supervisor. Example: precondition entry shows 1510 Pa. Rationale: dust collector condition affects air quality and blast cabinet function; pressure drop trend informs filter replacement planning in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   4.6. Drain and tag hydraulic or lubricant circuits where work will be performed; secure lines per MM-P3-L4-HT02 procedures. Rationale: prevents accidental release of hydraulic pressure and contamination of parts.
   4.7. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03 lubrication: verify lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 is the dispense material to be used for bearings and separator plates during reassembly. Rationale: using the specified lubricant ensures compatibility with blast media and avoids premature bearing failure.
   4.8. Perform verification walkdown with maintenance lead and safety officer to confirm all isolation points are controlled and areas are safe for entry. Rationale: face-to-face verification reduces communication errors.
   4.9. Perform maintenance tasks as defined on the attached work order and MM-P3-L4-HT02 preventive task lists. Rationale: ensures all required inspections, replacements, and adjustments are completed during the planned outage.

5. Examples of common maintenance activities to schedule during this shutdown
   5.1. Replace or inspect oven element connections and refractory panels per MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   5.2. Inspect conveyors on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 for wear and alignment; adjust clearances as required.
   5.3. On EQ-P3-L4-SB03, replace filters if pressure drop trend indicates near-limit readings; document filter serials in the record.
   5.4. Lubricate bearings using CFW-LUB-526; note batch or lot on maintenance record.

6. Records to keep
   6.1. Completed shutdown checklist with timestamps and initials for each isolation and verification step.
   6.2. Work order with completed tasks, parts used, and signatures of performing technicians and maintenance lead.
   6.3. Dust collector pressure drop readings before and after maintenance, including the precondition reading of 1510 Pa.
   6.4. Lubricant usage log showing CFW-LUB-526 used for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and quantity dispensed.
   6.5. Any non-conformance reports and corrective action plans created during the outage.
   6.6. Attachments or references to MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2 task pages executed during the shutdown.

7. Restart and verification
   7.1. Remove lockout/tagout only after all work is complete, tools and materials are cleared, and a final permit-to-start review is signed by the maintenance lead and safety officer.
   7.2. Re-energize systems in a controlled sequence per MM-P3-L4-HT02. Perform functional tests and run a validation piece through the heat treat process where required.
   7.3. Verify dust collector operation and confirm post-maintenance pressure drop is acceptable and recorded.

8. Sign-off
   8.1. Performed by: Lead Technician (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________
   8.2. Verified by: Maintenance Supervisor (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________
   8.3. Safety approval: Safety Officer (print name) ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________

9. References
   9.1. MM-P3-L4-HT02
   9.2. MM-P3-L4-HT02-S2
   9.3. SOP-P3-L4-01

Notes: Deviations from this SOP require documented approval and an updated risk assessment. Maintain all closure records in the document control system per site retention policy.
